jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Single-Molecule and Single-Vesicle Imaging of Neurodegenerative Diseases
jobs.description:
Are you interested in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases using cutting-edge fluorescence microscopy and single-vesicle imaging? Do you want to contribute to uncovering how protein aggregation and membrane interactions drive the development of Parkinson's disease? Then the Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University invites you to apply for a postdoctoral position within the ERC Starting Grant-funded project SPARTA.

We are seeking a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join our research group at the Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University. The successful candidate will develop and apply advanced single-molecule and single-vesicle imaging approaches to investigate the dynamic interactions between α-synuclein oligomers and biological membranes, aiming to uncover fundamental mechanisms of neurodegeneration and contribute to the development of novel strategies for early disease detection.

This is a fixed-term 2-year position starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will join the ERC Starting Grant-funded project SPARTA, aiming to uncover the molecular mechanisms of α-synuclein aggregation and membrane interactions in Parkinson’s disease.

The position will primarily involve:

• Investigating α-synuclein aggregation and interactions with lipid membranes.
• Developing and applying advanced single-molecule and single-vesicle fluorescence microscopy.
• Exploring how membrane composition and properties influence protein aggregation and membrane disruption.
• Performing quantitative image analysis and computational data analysis.
• Developing novel single-vesicle assays for studying neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.
The research will be conducted in an interdisciplinary environment at the Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, in collaboration with researchers in biophysics, molecular biology, and neuroscience.

Your profile
We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a strong background in experimental biophysics and quantitative fluorescence microscopy.

The ideal candidate should have:

• A PhD in nanoscience, biophysics, biochemistry, or a related field.
• Experience with single-molecule or single-vesicle fluorescence microscopy, preferably TIRF microscopy.
• Experience with lipid membranes, liposomes, or protein–membrane interactions.
• Strong skills in quantitative image analysis and data processing, preferably using Python.
• Experience in scientific publishing and communicating research findings.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment.
• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• Experience with α-synuclein, protein aggregation, or neurodegenerative diseases is an advantage but not a requirement.
We value scientific curiosity, creativity, independence, and a collaborative mindset.

Who we are
The Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University offers an international and interdisciplinary research environment with state-of-the-art facilities and strong collaborations.

The successful candidate will join the research group led by Assistant Professor Mette Galsgaard Malle, focusing on single-molecule and single-vesicle imaging to understand molecular interactions and disease mechanisms.

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the Department of Chemistry, Gustav Wieds Vej 14, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Assistant Professor Mette Galsgaard Malle, malle@inano.au.dk.

Deadline 
All applications must be received no later than 2 December 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Plant Biochemistry
jobs.description:
PhD Project in studying the molecular basis of flower color and patterns

  The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in AI-driven knowledge extraction for plant metabolism. The project is part of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars (Grant Agreement No. 101312557), funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Stripes&Stars trains ten doctoral candidates across eight European countries in modern breeding of ornamental and fruit crops, using flower and fruit colour – anthocyanins and other flavonoids in petunia, calibrachoa, poinsettia and bilberry – as its scientific showcase. The network brings together seven beneficiaries (TU Wien, Klemm + Sohn, Università Campus Bio-Medico, Utrecht University, University of Copenhagen, Lantana Bio, UiT The Arctic University of Norway) and associated partners at Galab, the University of Helsinki, the University of Amsterdam and Chulalongkorn University.

  The project

  Anthocyanins represents one of the most widespread plant pigments giving rise to the diverse colors to fruits, vegetables and flowers. Flower pigmentation is a critical trait guiding the attraction of pollinators. Some flowers develop remarkable patterns through spatial  accumulation of anthcocyanins in distinct and repetitive patterns. Yet, we still don’t know the molecular mechanisms governing flower patterns

  You will:

  -Develop a protoplast pipeline for isolation of cells derived from distinct flower petal patterns

  -Map the proteomes of different cell types

  -Employ biotin-dependent proximity labeling to map the protein networks of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway.

  -Elucidate regulatory proteins facilitating anthocyanin pathway assembly and disassembly.

  Planned Secondments: Klemm (1 month) to sample plant material from the flower diversity panel. TU Wien (Prof. Heidi Halbwirth, 2 months) for protoplast optimization for cell type protomics profiling and expression of fusion constructs. Lantana Bio (3 months) to translate findings to optimize a bioproduction process of tailored anthocyanins in yeast. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of Biology, chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology or biotechnology, who wish to join a dynamic research group working on plant biochemistry and biosynthesis of specialized metabolites. Applicants can have a background in elucidation/characterization of metabolic pathways, plant molecular biology/biochemistry, metabolic engineering or plant transformation.

  Important scientific values

  We will specifically select candidates displaying an open mindset, ability to collaborate within research teams and contribute to a healthy work environment. The candidate is encouraged to communicate their research openly with a curiosity towards different viewpoints and disciplines.

  MSCA guidelines

• You must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment. 	
• You may be of any nationality.   Our group and research- and what do we offer

  The successful applicant will join Tomas Laursen and the Dynamic Metabolons Research Group, which specializes in the organization of biosynthetic pathways for production of bioactive compounds. We combine microscopy, metabolomics and proteomics with fundamental biochemistry to study biosynthesis of plant specialized metabolites from the single enzyme- to the whole plant level. 

  The Dynamic Metabolons research Group is a part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, which hosts four Sections spanning from molecular biology to crop science and environmental chemistr. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories, plant growth facilities, and a metabolomics platform hosted within the Section. 

  The principal supervisor is Associate Professor Tomas Laursen, tola@plen.ku.dk.

If the latest degree has not been completed, please include a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records and a written statement from the institution or supervisor.

jobs.occupation: 2 PhD fellowships MSCA in AI-driven discovery of plant metabolic pathways
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for two PhD fellowships in AI-driven discovery of plant metabolic pathways – doctoral candidates DC7 and DC8 of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars. Both projects are part of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars (Grant Agreement No. 101312557), funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Stripes&Stars trains ten doctoral candidates across eight European countries in modern breeding of ornamental and fruit crops, using flower and fruit colour – anthocyanins and other flavonoids in petunia, calibrachoa, poinsettia and bilberry – as its scientific showcase. The network brings together seven beneficiaries (TU Wien, Klemm + Sohn, Università Campus Bio-Medico, Utrecht University, University of Copenhagen, Lantana Bio, UiT The Arctic University of Norway) and associated partners at Galab, the University of Helsinki, the University of Amsterdam and Chulalongkorn University. The University of Copenhagen hosts the network’s two data-science doctoral candidates (DC7 and DC8), who together provide the computational backbone for predictive colour and specialised-metabolite engineering.

  Start dates: DC7 is expected to start 1 June 2027 (month 3 of the network) and DC8 1 January 2028 (month 10 of the network), or as soon as possible thereafter. Please state in your application which project you are applying for; you may apply for both.

  Project DC7: Knowledge graph construction for specialised metabolite pathways (Stripes&Stars WP4–5)  Flavonoids and anthocyanins colour petunia flowers and bilberry fruit, protect plants against UV light and stress, and attract pollinators – and roughly 20% of the carbon flux in plants passes through the flavonoid pathway. Yet knowledge of the enzymes, transporters and regulators that control which pigment accumulates where is scattered across tens of thousands of papers. This project will make that knowledge computable.  You will:

   	
• Use the PlantConnectome large-language-model pipeline to extract and interlink knowledge on enzymes, substrates, transporters, transcription factors, stresses and genetic modifications that regulate pigment and specialised-metabolite biosynthesis, from more than 70,000 publications, into the first comprehensive knowledge graph of plant specialised-metabolite pathways 	
• Extend the graph to environmental context – in particular how concurrent stresses (e.g. high light with heat or drought) reshape pigment and specialised-metabolite accumulation, and whether the regulators involved are shared across ornamental and fruit species 	
• Apply symbolic reasoning and link prediction (e.g. AnyBURL rule mining and graph neural networks) to infer missing pathway components and regulatory relationships, yielding testable hypotheses and engineering targets for the experimental partners 	
• Build an interactive, ChatGPT-like interface to the graph, so that consortium members and the wider community can retrieve complete, evidence-linked information on genes, enzymes, pathways and phenotypes 	
• Work closely with DC8 (network-based pathway prediction, also at UCPH) so that graph and expression evidence are integrated into one explainable framework   Secondments: TU Wien (Prof. Heidi Halbwirth, 3 months) to integrate graph predictions with enzyme characterisation and pigment pathway analysis, and Klemm + Sohn (Stuttgart, 2 months) to validate predicted targets in an applied breeding context. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of bioinformatics, computer science, data science or computational biology, or plant biochemistry with a strong computational interest. Experience with natural language processing, large language models, graph databases or knowledge-graph reasoning is an advantage. An interest in plant metabolism is essential; a formal background in it is not.

  Project DC8: Multi-omics co-expression networks for predicting novel metabolic pathways (Stripes&Stars WP4–5)  Which genes make a petunia petal purple, a poinsettia bract white, or a bilberry flesh blue? Many of the enzymes, transporters and regulators are still unknown, and the ones we know were found one at a time. This project will find them systematically from expression data.  You will:

   	
• Build advanced co-expression and regulatory networks from consortium and public RNA-seq data using the group’s TEA-GCN algorithm, which aggregates linear and non-linear correlations across conditions to yield condition-specific, explainable networks 	
• Integrate cell- and tissue-resolved expression, proteomic and epigenomic datasets to delineate the regulatory subnetworks that drive pigment and specialised-metabolite production 	
• Combine these networks with the DC7 knowledge graph and explore neurosymbolic reasoning – coupling learned graph representations (graph neural networks, knowledge-graph embeddings) with symbolic rules mined from the literature graph – to infer missing pathway members and regulators with explanations a biologist can check 	
• Predict and prioritise engineering targets (regulators, enzymes, environmental cues) for experimental validation by the network’s experimental partners, and follow how those predictions fare 	
• Consolidate network- and graph-based predictions into a shared resource for the consortium   Secondment: University of Amsterdam (Prof. Ronald Koes, 3 months) to integrate transcriptomic and epigenetic datasets from petunia. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science or data science, or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with transcriptomics, network inference, graph machine learning or knowledge graphs is an advantage. An interest in plant metabolism is essential; a formal background in it is not.

  Eligibility and what we value  MSCA eligibility rules  This position is subject to the eligibility rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks:

   	
• Mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. 	
• You must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment. 	
• You may be of any nationality.   What we value  Coding experience is welcome but not required at entry – we teach it. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

   	
• questioning data rather than accepting it – asking what was measured, how, and against which expectation 	
• noticing anomalies and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting computational evidence to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are equally interested in candidates from biology who want to learn computation and candidates from computer science, physics or engineering who want to learn biology.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen.

jobs.occupation: Cargo Bike Delivery Rider (Part-Time) – Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Join MoveByBike

Do you enjoy being active instead of sitting behind a desk? Are you looking for flexible part-time work that fits around your studies or other commitments?

MoveByBike is looking for motivated E-Cargo Bike Riders to join our team in Copenhagen as soon as possible.

As an E-Cargo Bike Rider, you'll deliver food products, parcels, and other goods to businesses and private customers across Copenhagen using our modern electric cargo bikes. Every day is different, and you'll spend your shifts cycling through one of the world's most bike-friendly cities while helping keep Copenhagen moving.

No previous cargo bike experience is required, we provide full training before your first shift.

What you'll do

As part of our operations team, you will:

• 
Deliver goods safely and efficiently using our electric cargo bikes

• 
Load and unload deliveries at our Copenhagen base and customer locations

• 
Follow planned delivery routes throughout the city

• 
Provide friendly and professional service to our customers

• 
Follow safety procedures and traffic regulations

Who we're looking for

This role could be a great fit if you:

• 
Enjoy cycling and being physically active

• 
Like working independently while being part of a supportive team

• 
Are reliable, punctual, and take responsibility for your work

• 
Are comfortable working outdoors throughout the year

• 
Want flexible part-time work alongside your studies or other activities

Please note that this is an active outdoor job. You'll spend most of your shift cycling, loading and unloading goods, and working in a variety of weather conditions. If you enjoy staying active and don't mind the Danish weather, you'll likely enjoy working with us.

Requirements

• 
You are at least 18 years old

• 
You currently live in or near Copenhagen

• 
You are legally allowed to work in Denmark (a Danish CPR number is required before employment begins)

• 
You can communicate in English and/or Danish

• 
You are physically fit and able to perform manual work throughout your shift

• 
You are willing to follow schedules, safety procedures, and traffic laws

• 
Previous delivery experience is appreciated, but it is not a requirement

Working hours

• 
Flexible scheduling

• 
Negotiable minimum of hours per week (example: minimum 10 or 20 hours per week)

• 
Availability for at least one Monday shift each week is required, as Mondays are our busiest operating day

• 
Additional shifts available depending on your availability and company needs

• 
Shifts are available on most days between 07:00 and 22:00

Location

Our operational base is located in Nørrebro, which has excellent public transport connections to S-trains, buses and the Metro. It is also easy to reach via bike. All shifts start and end at our base.

The Department of Public Health at University of Copenhagen, Denmark, together with the The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomeds offers a Postdoctoral Fellowship position in causal inference with special focus on continuous-time causal inference, identification, and instrumental variables methods. 

  The anticipated hiring date is March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  About the Centre

  The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease.

  About the Section of Biostatistics
 The Section of Biostatistics carries out independent research in biostatistical applications and methods; it undertakes teaching of students at various educations, undergraduate as well as postgraduate, and it offers biostatistical advice to staff and students in all disciplines of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences. The section is internationally renowned for a high research level, especially within time-to-event analysis, while other competence areas include e.g. causal inference, latent variable modelling and prediction models. The section aims to maintain a strong position in these areas but also wants to expand into new areas of biostatistical research. The underlying idea is to produce high-level methodological research that is relevant in practical applications.

  More information on the Section of Biostatistics can be found at: https://biostat.ku.dk/. 
  

  Job Description
 We invite highly qualified, thorough, and motivated applicants to apply for a postdoctoral position in causal inference and statistical methodology. The successful candidate will conduct methodological research at the intersection of causal inference, event-history analysis, statistical machine learning, and semiparametric theory. Research will focus on the development of statistical methods for longitudinal and time-to-event data, with particular emphasis on continuously monitored data, dynamic treatment strategies, identification, and instrumental variable methods. Potential research directions include:  

   	
• causal inference for survival and competing risks outcomes 	
• continuous-time longitudinal causal models 	
• semiparametric and machine-learning-based estimation methods 	
• identification and estimation under instrumental variable assumptions 	
• methods for treatment switching, treatment discontinuation, and dynamic treatment interventions 	
• development of efficient and robust estimators for causal effects under complex longitudinal data structures   Example projects include the development of methods for causal inference with continuously observed treatment processes, incorporation of instrumental variables into survival analysis, and machine-learning-based estimation procedures for time-varying treatment effects. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute both theoretically and computationally, including development of new methodology, investigation of statistical properties, implementation of software, simulation studies, and applications to biomedical research questions. The candidate must participate in the interdisciplinary and dynamic research environment within the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed. The successful applicant is also encouraged to develop independent research directions aligned with the overall goals of the centre.

  The specific tasks of the position will include:

   	
• Manage own academic research and administrative activities. 	
• Conduct research in line with the goals of SMARTBiomed. 	
• Lead write-up of research papers pertaining to their own work and collaborate in the preparation of research publications. Ensure, where appropriate, that software research outputs are provided to ensure maximum utility. 	
• Present papers at conferences or public meetings. 	
• Contribute to the administrative activities of SMARTBiomed and the research group of appointment.   The postdoctoral fellow will also be encouraged and mentored to develop new proposals and research initiatives to support additional research. Over the course of the position, opportunities to teach at either the graduate or undergraduate level exist.

 Essential experience and skills:

   	
• A Ph.D. in Statistics/Biostatistics, or similar disciplines.  	
• Strong skills in theoretical methods development.  	
• Experience and interest in data analysis and programming (e.g., in R) is further highly desirable.  	
• Strong English, scientific writing, and oral communications skills 	
• The ability to work independently, effectively, and collaboratively.    

  Terms of employment 
 The position is fixed term, limited to a period of 2 years, with the potential for up to one additional year, as needed to finish ongoing work. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

Currently, the monthly salary starts at 36,877.42 DKK/approx. 4,933.00 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Questions
 More information about the positions is available by contacting Associate Professor Helene Rytgaard, Section of Biostatistics, hely@sund.ku.dk, Professor Erin Gabriel, Section of Biostatistics, erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk, or Professor Torben Martinussen, Section of Biostatistics, tma@sund.ku.dk.

You will provide practical and technical support for research and teaching in underwater technology and help ensure that researchers and students have reliable, well-documented equipment for laboratory and field activities.

Your work tasks
You will become part of the underwater technology research environment at Aalborg University Energy in Esbjerg, where research projects combine the development, testing and application of advanced underwater robotic systems. The position provides shared technical support across several projects and contributes to coherent mechanical and electronic design practices. In this way, you will help researchers reduce duplicated technical work, strengthen knowledge sharing and reuse proven solutions across research activities.

You will work closely with researchers, students and external collaborators in a role that combines independent technical responsibility with day-to-day collaboration. Your work will take place in laboratories, workshops and field settings, depending on the activities and testing needs of the research projects. A central part of the role is to make equipment ready for use, keep it operational and support colleagues in using it safely and effectively.

You will develop laboratory and field-testing setups for underwater robotic systems, including selecting, integrating and maintaining relevant instrumentation, data acquisition equipment and data-logging systems. You will conduct laboratory and field tests involving underwater vehicles and associated sensors, support the standardisation and maintenance of electrical and mechanical hardware, and contribute to the design, development and fabrication of new components. You will also prepare user manuals and technical documentation, assist students in the operation of equipment, and help ensure that technical solutions remain accessible and reusable across projects.

You have a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electronics or a related technical field. You are familiar with control electronics, instrumentation, data acquisition and data-logging systems, and you can use computer-aided design tools to develop and document mechanical solutions.

You have experience with robotic testing equipment and understand the importance of reliable instrumentation, systematic test procedures and clear technical documentation. Experience with the Robot Operating System or a comparable robotics framework, as well as MATLAB for data processing and analysis, is required. jobs.occupation: PhD in Electrolyte Solvation and Interphase Engineering for Rechargeable Calcium Batteries
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from 1st of March 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks
You will develop and investigate non-aqueous liquid electrolytes for rechargeable calcium batteries, focusing on how Ca2+ solvation, ion pairing and interphase formation govern electrochemical reversibility. Your work will contribute to a complementary research programme on calcium-battery electrode materials and cell development at AAU Energy.

You will systematically vary salt chemistry, solvent composition and concentration within selected electrolyte families. Physicochemical measurements and spectroscopic analysis will be used to examine electrolyte coordination environments and ion association. These investigations will guide the selection of formulations for detailed electrochemical and interfacial studies.

A central part of the work will be the design and evaluation of calcium plating and stripping experiments, including measurements of coulombic efficiency, polarization and cycling stability under defined conditions. You will use appropriate controls and complementary analyses to verify metallic calcium deposition and distinguish it from electrolyte decomposition or other electrochemical reactions. You will investigate electrode interphase composition and evolution using XPS, supported by electron microscopy and, where appropriate, ToF-SIMS for morphology and species distribution. Raman spectroscopy, complemented by NMR where relevant, will probe electrolyte coordination and ion association. Targeted MD simulations may clarify Ca²⁺ solvation and ion pairing. Correlating these findings with electrochemical performance will establish mechanism-based guidelines for electrolyte formulation and selection.

Working closely with the PhD researcher developing cathode and calcium-alloying anode materials, you will assess selected electrode–electrolyte combinations and contribute to reproducible coin-cell evaluation. You will also contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, teaching, supervision of student projects and departmental dissemination activities.

The position is offered in relation to the Batteries research group, and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Power Electronics Systems Integration and Materials”.

Your competencies 
Applicants are expected to hold an M.Sc. degree in chemistry, materials science, physics, chemical engineering, or a closely related discipline. Candidates should have a solid scientific background and preferably hands-on experience in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, electrolyte formulation and preparation, battery testing and characterization, or the handling of air- and moisture-sensitive materials under controlled environments. A strong interest in electrochemical energy storage, interfacial chemistry, spectroscopic characterization techniques, and quantitative experimental data analysis is highly desirable.

Experience with advanced characterization techniques, particularly spectroscopy and surface analysis, will be considered an advantage. Familiarity with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations or other computational approaches for investigating electrolyte properties is beneficial but not essential, as the position is primarily focused on experimental research.

Excellent written and spoken English communication skills, together with the ability to collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary and international research environment, are essential.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real world energy challenges.

Aalborg University has been ranked as the best university in Europe within energy research and is among the very best universities worldwide in this field. At AAU Energy you will be part of a top international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges such as the green transition and future energy systems.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and with diverse national and disciplinary backgrounds, which creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as working language in both research and teaching, which supports the integration of international colleagues.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. jobs.occupation: Outsourcing Project Director - Drug Substance Outsourcing
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Project Director, you will lead the most complex sourcing projects in Drug Substance, from category strategy through to signed contracts with CMOs, where commitments can exceed DKK 1 billion. You will shape strategies for areas of growing importance to Novo, such as synthetic peptides, and negotiate partnerships that are strong commercially and sustainable over time. Your work helps keep the supply of treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases reliable.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior sourcing and project leader who combines a strategic mindset with an eye for contractual detail.

**You Have

**

• A university master’s degree in pharmacy, biology, engineering, supply chain management, law or business.

• Around 15+ years of relevant pharmaceutical experience, in manufacturing, manufacturing development and/or CMO environments. The role may suit candidates with around 20 years of experience.

• A strong background in strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and external partner management.

• Solid experience leading complex, cross-functional projects, as project and/or line manager.

• In-depth knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing, CMOs, quality and regulatory requirements.

• Excellent negotiation and contracting skills, and the ability to engage with senior management and CMO executives, up to CEO level.

• The ability to lead and influence without formal authority, with resilience, autonomy, a sense of urgency and strong execution skills.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Supplementary training in areas such as cGMP, project execution or personal development.

• An existing network within Novo, CMOs and pharmaceutical engineering companies.

• Experience in Drug Product sourcing.

What you’ll do

You will own sourcing projects from the first idea to final implementation, and you will keep strategy, contract and delivery pointing in the same direction.

**In Practice, You Will

**

• Develop category strategies for areas of strategic importance, such as synthetic peptides, by pairing market insight, including global players and trends, with Novo’s strategic outlook.

• Lead critical CMO negotiations independently until signature, securing outcomes within mandate that balance value, cost, flexibility, speed and risk.

• Drive projects end-to-end: set up governance and Steering Committees, build business cases and plans, define deliverables and manage risk.

• Bring together specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance and Legal, and raise bottlenecks early so work keeps moving.

• Keep SVP and EVP-level stakeholders informed and aligned on progress, and give input to business plans and budgets.

• Raise the standard for how Drug Substance Outsourcing works by sharing your approach with category managers and developing sourcing standards.

Who you’ll work with

You will be a senior individual contributor in GSOD Drug Substance Outsourcing, reporting to the Senior Director of the department. The role has no direct reports, but you will lead through influence: category groups and project teams with specialists from MSAT, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Quality, Finance and Legal, as well as colleagues in Global Contract Manufacturing DS, Supply Chain Design, GMS Management and country affiliates.

Externally, you will work with CMOs across the US, Europe and Asia, so you should expect to spend significant time abroad. You will balance partnership and long-term collaboration with the best possible commercial terms for Novo, and you will be at ease handling cross-cultural discussions when tension runs high.

In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. Your primary focus will be Drug Substance, with potential involvement in Drug Product and Devices.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take decisions independently and to give strategic guidance to senior leaders on the project portfolio. You will build new skills through cross-functional and cross-border work, and you will be recognised for results through clear performance expectations.

You will also have room to challenge convention: to find faster, better ways to run projects and to shape new processes and standards for CMO partnerships.

The pay range for this role is 940,800 – 1,448,700 DKK per year. The final offer reflects your experience and qualifications.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Novo’s most strategic CMO partnerships from strategy to signature, apply for the Project Director role by 19st November 2026 . We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer (AI, OCR/IDP & Automation)
jobs.description:
Build intelligent financial products. Solve real problems. Shape a company.

For our client Verifi Finance in central Copenhagen, we’re looking for an entrepreneurial Senior Software Engineer who combines exceptional engineering skills with a strong sense of ownership and a drive to solve meaningful customer problems.

At Verifi Finance, they believe great software starts with understanding the problem, not writing the code. They are building an AI-native platform that transforms complex, manual accounting workflows into reliable, intelligent automation — helping finance teams spend less time validating data and more time creating value.

This isn’t a role where you’ll simply pick up tickets and implement predefined solutions. You’ll work closely with their founders and customers to uncover problems worth solving, challenge assumptions, shape the product, and take ideas from concept to production.

You’ll have the opportunity to influence technical decisions, build across the stack, experiment with emerging AI capabilities, and help define how they build and scale the company

Verifi Finance has solid funding and excisting customers in Denmark and Sweden with plans to expand across Europe soon.

See more here: verifi.finance

The Challenge (What you will build)

You will dive deep into the day-to-day chaos of accounting workflows, extract the logic, and write software that automates, validates, and quality-controls financial data.

• The “Hardcore” Logic:

You will translate messy, human-centric accounting processes into strict, “hardcore” business logic. This requires understanding the why behind a transaction, not just the how.

You will build pipelines that ingest raw financial documents, cleaning and structuring that data for their system.

You will build AI agents that don’t just “chat”, but take real-world actions and amaze users to their core.

You will identify bottlenecks in Verifi Finance’s customers’ daily lives and code them out of existence.

You will not shy away from contributing to UX and state management (client side) of the product.

• Core: TypeScript (Must be god-level). They value type safety and strict standards.

• Data: Deep understanding of Databases. You know how to model financial ledgers and ensure data integrity.

• AI-Assisted Workflow: At Verifi, they move fast. They expect you to be proficient with Cursor, Claude, and Gemini to accelerate boilerplate and refactoring. They’d love to see how you do it your way.

• The “Plus” List: Experience with Python, Go, Rust, or Java is highly valued for backend performance and data processing_.

Who You Are

• Direct & Energetic: You cut through the noise. You communicate clearly, you push back when the design is wrong, and you bring energy to the team.

• Customer-Obsessed: You are willing to understand the “boring” parts of accounting to build the exciting parts of the software. You empathize with the user’s pain.

• A “Finisher”: You don’t just start cool experiments; you ship production-ready, test-covered features.

• Adaptable: Verifi Finance is well funded and ready to roll. The environment changes, the vision evolves, and you need to be quick to absorb new knowledge.

• Startup Mindset: Previous experience working in a startup environment is a strong plus.

• A unique opportunity to contribute to building a breakthrough financial software system

• Close collaboration with the founders and a team of dedicated colleagues

• Hybrid workplace with expected 2-3 workdays per week at the office

• A dynamic work environment with short decision-making paths

• Strong opportunities for personal development and expanded responsibilities

• Competitive salary and benefits package. They have an ESOP in place and this role is planned to be a part of it with standard cliff periods.

You will work at the company HQ in central Copenhagen, offering lunch facilities and access to a vibrant startup ecosystem.

jobs.occupation: Senior Engineer – AI & Data Products (Aarhus)
jobs.description:
The Tech Collective, Data & AI

Kalkværksvej 5, 8000 Aarhus · Full-time

We’re looking for a senior builder who turns AI and data into products people actually use. You’ve shipped real systems end to end, you know AI or data well enough to make it work in production, not just in a demo, and AI is as much a part of how you build as what you build.

What you'll do

In this role, you’ll take client ideas from a rough hypothesis to a working prototype, and then to a production system that runs reliably. You'll design the architecture, write the code across frontend, backend, and data, and decide what to build and what to leave out. It's a hands-on role. Most of your time goes into building, and the rest goes into working with clients to make sure you’re building the right thing.

The work covers generative AI applications and agents, including the harnesses that make them reliable (tools, context, memory, orchestration, and guardrails), along with retrieval pipelines and the data flows they depend on. You’ll connect these to client systems, deploy them in the cloud, and set up the evals and observability you need to see whether they work and how to improve them. You’ll work closely with our data platform and AI specialists, review code, and help less experienced engineers grow.

What you'll bring

You're a builder at heart. You have a master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, (preferably) 5+ years of hands-on software experience, and a track record of shipping production-ready software systems. Ideally, you also have experience with the whole software development lifecycle: starting with an idea (whether your own or a stakeholder’s), designing the solution architecture, developing and testing the solution, and putting it into the hands of actual users. Good engineering matters to you, but you’re not a purist, you care more about shipping something that works and solves the problem.

What sets you apart is depth beyond the code. You know AI (LLMs, agents, RAG, evals) and data (data modelling, pipelines, event-driven, and real-time systems) well enough that others come to you for it. Ideally, you know a bit of both.

You're equally at home building AI products and building with AI. Coding agents and AI-assisted tools are part of how you work every day, and you use them critically. You know where they make you faster and where the output needs a careful human eye.

To be a great fit, it helps if you have:

• 
Solid full-stack skills in Python and/or TypeScript (e.g., React, Next.js, FastAPI), with production systems to show for it

• 
Hands-on experience building agents and the harnesses around them (tool use, MCP, context and memory management, orchestration, guardrails), and designing the data models and pipelines that real products run on

• 
An AI-native way of working, using coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex in your own development workflow, with a clear view of where they help and where they don’t

• 
Experience deploying and running solutions on AWS, Azure, or GCP, including containers, CI/CD, and enough observability to know what's going on

• 
System-level judgement: you can reason about architecture, trade-offs, and failure modes, and you can spot the weak points in an existing stack

• 
Curiosity about the client’s problem, and the ability to explain technical choices clearly to people who don’t write code

• 
A habit of helping others get better through sparring, pairing, and code reviews

English is our corporate language. Proficiency in one or more additional languages is a plus.

What we offer

At The Tech Collective, you’ll join a team of 30 consultants that feels closer to a nerdy startup than a large consultancy, while being firmly backed by Implement Consulting Group. You’ll own what you build, and you’ll have the freedom to shape your role in the direction that motivates you.

You’ll work on data and AI problems across industries, alongside experienced peers in AI, data, and software. Our culture is built on trust, curiosity, humility, and impact, with high autonomy, co-creation, and active knowledge-sharing.

Ready to build with us? We review applications on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as you can.

About The Tech Collective

The Tech Collective is a fast-growing consulting company powered by Implement Consulting Group. We help organisations unlock the potential of data, AI, and analytics so they’re fit for the digital future. In our collective, you’ll find people who combine nerdiness with infectious energy. We’re passionate about technology, and we have a sincere interest in people

For more than 50 years, KMD has built and operated digital infrastructure that citizens, governments, and businesses rely on from welfare and public administration to critical digital services.

As societies face demographic change, digital sovereignty, climate resilience, and technological disruption, we combine technology expertise with an understanding of society’s needs.

Our 2030 strategy and new cross-functional organization bring us closer to customers, combining domain expertise and technologies such as AI to create value for customers and society. We’re looking for an experienced Lead Learning & Development specialist to translate strategy into people initiatives and strengthen the employee experience across the People agenda.

About the Capability Management team

You will join our Capability Management team within the People (HR) department. We are accountable for onboarding, leadership and specialist development, strategic workforce planning, diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI), employee engagement, and performance management. We work closely with our lines of business and colleagues across People to translate business priorities into practical initiatives that build the capabilities KMD needs today and in the future.

ABOUT THE JOB

Working closely with business leaders and People teams, you will ensure our learning programs and offerings align with organizational goals, reinforce key competencies, and foster a thriving leadership culture. Your primary focus will be designing leadership development frameworks and taking end-to-end ownership of program implementation and delivery. Facilitation is a supporting part of the role, rather than its main focus.

Accountability and Key Responsibilities

Leadership development & frameworks

• 
Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of KMD’s leadership framework and principles, translating them into impactful learning offerings – from comprehensive development programs and focused learning sessions to bite-sized digital learning.

• 
Translate business strategy and cultural priorities into scalable leadership development programs and learning events for different leadership levels.

Program design & delivery

• 
Own the end-to-end design, implementation, and delivery of leadership development programs, translating frameworks into practical learning journeys and coordinating internal experts and external providers.

• 
Act as subject matter expert and advisor to leaders on leadership capability building.

Succession planning

• 
Own the succession planning framework and annual process in collaboration with HRBPs and business leaders.

• 
Ensure robust identification, assessment, and development of critical leadership talent and successors.

Assessment tools & development

• 
Lead the use and continuous improvement of Deeper Signals and Hogan to support individual and team development.

• 
Facilitate individual feedback sessions and team workshops, translating assessment insights into clear development actions.

Data, governance & impact

• 
Define success metrics for leadership development and succession planning.

• 
Use data and insights to continuously improve programs and ensure measurable impact.

You will work from our Ballerup office in reference to Head of Capability Management.

ABOUT YOU

Qualifications & Requirements

This role requires experience with end-to-end responsibility for designing, rolling out, and following up on leadership learning events and programs. Your core strength is designing leadership development frameworks and translating them into effective programs. You are experienced in defining clear learning objectives aligned with strategic goals and bring proven expertise in applying learning taxonomies to program design. We are looking for a framework architect and program owner, rather than primarily a facilitator.

• 
Over 5 years of experience in Learning & Development, with a strong emphasis on leadership development.

• 
Strong framework and learning design skills, combined with the ability to manage program delivery; facilitation, coaching, and communication skills support this work.

• 
Ability to manage multiple initiatives and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Ability to influence and build relationships across all levels of the cross-functional organization.

• 
Demonstrates empathy and emotional intelligence in interactions with learners and leaders.

• 
Relevant Master’s degree in HR, Organizational Development, Psychology, or a related field.
